title: Add invocation thermograph and log-cohort correlation for long-tail alerting
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary: Introduce an 'Invocation Thermograph' metric and dashboard along with a light-weight log-cohort correlation layer and KV-trace anchoring sampler to improve detection and triage of long-tail latency/cost regressions.
Motivation: Existing alert signals surface percentile spikes but miss gradual slope-driven regressions and correlated log patterns that indicate workload shifts (e.g., prompt length or repeated reruns). The thermograph visualizes invocation density across token-cost vs latency slices over time, enabling SREs/product teams to see heating/cooling patterns and isolate cohorts.
Design:
- New metric pipeline that emits invocation_thermograph_bucket{tenant,model,segment} representing counts in 2D microbins (token-cost, latency) aggregated per minute; bins are compact (64 bins) and encoded as base64 for transport.
- KV-trace anchoring sampler: sampled traces attach compact KV-hitmap for first-10-kv-keys to help link cache miss patterns to thermograph hot bins.
- Log-cohort correlation: a lightweight offline join that correlates thermograph hot bins with log cohort signatures (e.g., prompt templates, feature flags) to produce 'cohort tags' for follow-up traces.
- Dashboard: new 'Invocation Thermograph' tile, cohort scatter, and a slope-alert tuning panel.
- Alerting: new SLO rule 'thermograph-slope' that triggers when a bin's occupancy increases with a sustained positive slope over N windows; alerts are debounced by cohort density and paired with a recommended follow-up query.
Rollout: feature-flag rollout over 3 weeks: 10% tenants -> 50% -> all.
Defaults: sampling weight 0.02, thermograph retention 30d for hot bins rollups.

Review conversation:
- Marco Li (request changes): "CPU profile shows ~8% p99 increase in encode path for 64-bin payloads; can we reduce copies and add a streaming encoder?"
- Author (Priya): "Addressed in perf commit: switching to a pooled buffer and streaming varint encoding; re-ran bench and p99 regression gone (see bench results in comments)."
- Elena (comment): "Nice dashboard; add an example follow-up LogQL query in the runbook so on-call knows where to start."
- Author: "Added example queries and a small playbook entry with steps (isolate tenant, pull sampled KV-anchor traces, run cohort-affinity join)."
- Omar (approval): "Approach LGTM. Verified alert firing simulation in staging; no noisy alerts at 10% rollout."
CI checks: ["unit: pass","integration/ingest: pass","lint: pass","e2e-dashboard-snapshot: pass","bench: pass"]
Testing notes: unit tests added for encoder edge-cases (empty/oversize buckets), integration test validates payload flow from ingest -> store -> dashboard rollups; e2e sim creates artificial hot bin and verifies alert fires under simulated slope.
Observed perf: microbench reduces allocation churn by ~40% and keeps CPU p99 within 1% of baseline in our sandbox.
Rollback plan: revert feature flag and remove alert rule if noisy; code change is backward compatible with metric schema versioning.
Runbook excerpts (added to docs file):
- How to query a hot bin: SELECT decode_bin(thermograph_payload) WHERE tenant = X AND bin = Y;
- Recommended follow-up: fetch sampled traces with kv_anchor.tag = bin:Y and run cohort-affinity to list top prompt templates.
Migration / Storage: payloads are stored in existing metrics blob store; retention and rollups configured via pipeline flags; no DB migration required.
Backwards compatibility: consumers not opting into thermograph will ignore new metric series.
Release notes: "Adds Invocation Thermograph metric, dashboard, and slope-based alerting to improve detection of gradual long-tail regressions. Opt-in rollout under feature flag; low-overhead sampling and encoder optimizations added to mitigate CPU impact."
